title: Add anonymous classes to GDScript
body:
- Bugsquad edit: Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10132

Adds Java-style anonymous classes to GDScript, a one-off subclass declared inline at a instantiation;

```gdscript
var timer = Timer.new():
    func _ready():
        print("<debug anon timer init>")
        wait_time = 2.0
        autostart = true
```

> Each `.new():` body creates a new class the same way the `class` keyword or a separate script would, just declared right where it's instantiated. Existing class infrastructure (members, fqcn, inheritance) is reused, with no new AST nodes or bytecodes.

## Disclosure:

I've used AI, specifically Claude 4.6 to write the unit tests. I didn't know of their existence in the first place.
Similarly, I've used it as an encyclopedic source of tidbits and quirks I don't think I could've ever learned of by myself at least until I would've bumped into them.
The code has been in the making for a bit over a year on and off as I learned about the engine.

## Motivation/Reasoning

Short, local specializations of a class currently require either:
- declaring a separate inner class outside of the function it's meant to be in (hurts readability)
- assigning callables to every hook, retroactively whenever a new function needs overriding. (stylistically unpleasant and a hog on productivity)

Anonymous classes make it natural to override one or two methods for a
single instance, it greatly improves your ability to customize behavior for a multitude of extending classes whose changes don't warrant having their own file.

The `class` keyword for inner classes is useful if one is to have multiple instances. But that isn't needed in those use cases. and requires declaring it outside of functions.
External files similarly hurt readability and require you to know where in a script does this file see use.

## Syntax

The body can be multi-line;

```gdscript
var b = ItemSword.new():
    var rightful_owner : Variant
    func get_name() -> String:
        if owner != null and rightful_owner == owner:
            return "awoken " + super().get_name()
        else:
            return  "dormant " + super().get_name()
```

...or inline (single `func`)

```gdscript
var btn = Button.new(): func _pressed(): print("clicked")
```

It works in any expression context (call args, array literals,
parenthesised conditions):

```gdscript
connect(SomeHandler.new(): func handle(): ...)
if (Base.new(): func ok() -> bool: return true).ok():
    ...
```

The base class can be any identifier chain (`Outer.Inner.new():`) or a
`preload("...").new():`. Constructor arguments are forwarded to the base's
`_init`.

## Current Implementation

Concentrated in `modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp` (`parse_call`).
After `.new(args)` the parser checks for a `:` and, if present, builds a
synthetic `ClassNode` named `@AnonymousClass_<Base>_<N>`, parses a class
body, registers it as an inner class of the enclosing scope, and
rewrites the callee so the `.new()` instantiates the synthetic class.

A small `outer_colon_reserved` flag prevents the `:` being stolen from
outer contexts that own it (`for ... in ...:`, `if ...:`, `while ...:`, `match
…:`, and `{ key: value }` dictionaries). Grouping expressions (`()`,
`[]`, `{}`, call arg lists, subscripts) reset the flag since they start
a fresh expression scope.

Error messages use a new `GDScript::get_display_name()` that turns the
synthetic name into `(anonymous Base at line N)` so stack traces stay
readable.

## Unit Tests

`modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/parser/`:
- `features/anonymous_class.gd` : core behavior (override, ctor args,
  new members, typed assignment, dotted bases, nested, preloads).
- `features/anonymous_class_inline.gd` : inline / expression forms.
- `errors/anonymous_class_empty.gd`, `errors/anonymous_class_extends.gd` : error paths.

The current GDScript test suite still passes.

## Known limits

- Inline form accepts a single `func` only; multi-member bodies must use
  an indented block.
- Without parentheses, `if Base.new(): func ... : ...` is ambiguous,
  the `if` wins; users must wrap the anonymous class in `()` to reach
  into it.
- `load(path).new():` is not supported (only `preload`), because the
  base class has to be known at parse time.

## Current ideas:
have a custom keyword, like `modified` would simplify things; 
```gdscript
var anon_class = modified Base:
    func somefunc():
        #[...]
```
It would reduce line count and remove lines to catch edge cases like structures consuming colons, but i doubt it would be a wise idea to make it that much different from java's implementation.
